tools.name: vmcp-ast
tools.description: [CORE INFRASTRUCTURE / INVOKE FIRST] Ultra-fast AST code structure analyzer. When taking over a project, locating definitions, or assessing refactoring impact, you MUST prioritize this tool to establish global/local context. It returns a dehydrated structural map with exact line numbers in a single call, heavily replacing traditional grep searches.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Target path. Supports a single file/directory, or multiple paths separated by newlines (\n). Required for a fresh search, but omitted when requesting a later page with cache_id.

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Whether to scan subdirectories recursively when a directory is encountered (default: false). Keep this false if you only need shallow entry points of the current directory.

parameters.name: ignore
parameters.description: Enable default blacklist and scoped .gitignore rules (default: true). STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to keep enabled to prevent context explosion, unless you explicitly need to inspect build artifacts like target/dist.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Extension filter, comma-separated (e.g., js,ts,rs). When scanning large directories, it is STRONGLY RECOMMENDED to explicitly specify 'ext' to avoid hitting irrelevant files and triggering the 5000-file circuit breaker limit.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: Include Doc comments of functions in the structural output (default: false). Keep false if you only need line numbers for routing; set to true if understanding complex business logic is required.

parameters.name: cache_id
parameters.description: Pagination cache identifier returned by a previous truncated search. Use this instead of path when requesting another page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to fetch from a cached paginated result (default: 1).

parameters.name: truncate_chars
parameters.description: Character budget per page (default: 20000). Do not override this unless the user explicitly requests a different budget or the prompt specifically requires it; the default is recommended.

parameters.name: cache_ttl_sec
parameters.description: Optional cache lifetime in seconds for paginated results. When omitted, the system default is used and values above the configured maximum are clamped automatically.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. EXPLORE FIRST: ALWAYS invoke this tool before executing file reads (read_file) or text searches (grep/rg). Use the precise line numbers and AST signatures as anchors for your next steps. 2. ANTI-EXPLOSION: This tool has a strict 5000-file circuit breaker limit for matched files and allows at most 20 explicitly listed files in one call; do not mix file paths and directory paths. 3. PAGINATION: Large results may be paginated with cache_id + page. 4. BUDGET CONTROL: truncate_chars defaults to 20000 and should not be overridden unless the user explicitly asks for a different budget or the prompt requires it.

tools.name: vmcp-rg
tools.description: [TEXT-TO-STRUCTURE BRIDGE] Run ripgrep first, then map matched lines back to the most relevant AST structures. Use this when vmcp-ast alone is too broad and you need only the class/function context that directly contains a regex hit.

parameters.name: dir
parameters.description: Target directory to search recursively. This parameter is required for a fresh search and must point to an existing directory.

parameters.name: ext
parameters.description: Optional extension filter, comma-separated (e.g., lua,rs,ts). When omitted, rg searches all files and vmcp-rg keeps only files that vmcp-ast can structurally analyze.

parameters.name: rg_pattern
parameters.description: Ripgrep regex used for the first-pass text search. This parameter is required for a fresh search.

parameters.name: cache_id
parameters.description: Pagination cache identifier returned by a previous truncated vmcp-rg search. Use this instead of dir/ext/rg_pattern when requesting another page.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to fetch from a cached paginated result (default: 1).

parameters.name: truncate_chars
parameters.description: Character budget per page (default: 20000). Increase only when the user explicitly asks for a larger structural window.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. USE THIS AFTER YOU KNOW THE TEXT SIGNAL: vmcp-rg is for regex-to-structure narrowing, not for first-pass repository exploration. 2. SEARCH FLOW: it runs rg first and then only scans matched files with vmcp-ast internals. 3. OUTPUT RULE: only structures directly related to the matched lines are returned. Declaration hits expand that declaration structure; body hits collapse to the nearest relevant function/method context. 4. PAGINATION: large results may be paginated with cache_id + page.

tools.name: vmcp-patch
tools.description: [FUNCTION-LEVEL AST PATCHER] Re-locate a function or method by structural selector and replace the full function source. Use this when line numbers are stale and you need AST-based function replacement instead of raw text patching.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Target file that contains the function to patch. This parameter is required and must point to a regular file.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Flexible structural selector for a function or method, for example with_vmm, McpServer/with_vmm, or impl McpServer/with_vmm. If multiple nodes match, the tool returns more specific candidates instead of patching blindly.

parameters.name: replacement
parameters.description: Replacement source text. It must be the complete function source, starting from the declaration line. Body-only fragments are rejected.

tools.prompt: [OPERATION PROTOCOL] 1. PATCH FUNCTIONS ONLY: this tool only replaces function or method nodes, never type names or field identifiers. 2. STRICT INPUT RULE: always pass the complete function source starting from the declaration line; do not pass mode and do not pass body-only fragments. Requests that do not follow this rule are rejected. 3. SELECTOR FLOW: pass the loosest selector first; if multiple nodes match, the tool will return more specific structural candidates. 4. SAFETY: patches are written through a temp-file + rollback flow, validated by generic AST re-scan, ast-grep ERROR-node detection, and target identity re-location before the write is accepted.
